title: Traoré Warns Rivals 'No Two Captains on One Ship' Amid Reports of Junta Power Struggle
detail: Reports crystallized in mid-to-late July 2026 around an internal power struggle within Burkina Faso's ruling junta. Oumarou Yabré — intelligence chief and National Security Council head, considered the regime's #2 official — had not been seen publicly since late May 2026, stopped attending his office at the National Intelligence Agency, and had his home security detail reportedly cut. Junta spokesman Farouk Azaria Sorgho (considered #3) has also been absent since mid-May, with security sources alleging he was 'abducted' by Traoré associates (unconfirmed officially); infrastructure minister Adama Luc Sorgho was reportedly arrested. On a public visit to Ouahigouya on July 16, Capt. Ibrahim Traoré declared 'There can't be two captains on one ship' — widely read as a direct warning to internal rivals. Multiple outlets note that Imam Mohamed Ishaq Kindo, detained since May 26, 2026, is described as a close associate of Yabré — tying the religious crackdown (Grand Mosque closure, Religious Freedoms Law passed June 20) directly to the elite power struggle rather than religious policy alone.
